about: The scope notes of the finding aids, one per class of the classification: a hand file of librarian@PrompTugal.dinis. scope is one plain sentence on what the collection is; arranged says how its cards are ordered; kept_by names who looks after it (leave out to take the two agents that made most of its cards). The generator reads this file and never writes it.

GEN.scope: The repository's own front files: the rules (CLAUDE.md), the brief and its corrections, REALITY.md, the readmes and the board's top files.
GEN.arranged: By call number: the subclass (rules, brief, reality, readme, board), then the file's own short name.

PUB.scope: The publication: the pages readers see (the front page, site pages, lists, the newsroom section, the brand) and the articles, each signed and sourced.
PUB.arranged: By call number: articles, front page, lists, newsroom pages, site pages and the brand each have a subclass; within it by the page's short name.
PUB.kept_by: journalist@ for the articles, dev.pages@ for the pages

DAT.scope: Data and the ontology: the pages of companies, events, people, organisations, places and topics, and the schemas and ontology that give them their shape. The entity pages are catalogued but are not single nodes in the library graph; a connection to one ends at its collection.
DAT.arranged: By call number: one subclass for each kind of entity, then the entity's own short name.

BLD.scope: Build, code and release: the tools the board holds and the asset code; the build and the gate themselves are dev@'s and are catalogued only where the board names them.
BLD.arranged: By call number: tools, features, the gate, CI and asset code each have a subclass.

TEAM.scope: Agents, roles and keys: one card for each agent, each role's own files, the agent behaviour policies, the inboxes (the box, never its contents), run reports, budgets and the schedule.
TEAM.arranged: By call number: agents, roles, policies, inboxes, runs, budgets, keys and schedule each have a subclass.
TEAM.kept_by: conductor@ for the team, abp@ for the policies

WRK.scope: Work in hand: passes (focused rounds of work) and their findings, decisions, plans, briefs, tasks, desks and the story projects.
WRK.arranged: By call number: passes, findings, decisions, plans, briefs, tasks, desks and stories each have a subclass.

GDN.scope: Guidance, a special collection: Dinis's night memos, the ideas ledger with each idea in his words, the open questions and the named concepts. His words are never edited.
GDN.arranged: By call number: memos, ideas, questions and concepts each have a subclass; an idea is filed under its ledger number.

EVD.scope: Evidence and sources: captures and the vaults named by the board (by name only, never an address or a key).
EVD.arranged: By call number: sources, vaults and captures each have a subclass.

RDR.scope: Readers and observability: what the synthetic and guide readers found, and the read counter's own files.
RDR.arranged: By call number: observability, synthetic readers and the reader's guide each have a subclass.

LIB.scope: The library itself: its commission, architecture, catalogue, authority file, reality tree, desk and this finding aid.
LIB.arranged: By call number: the catalogue, authority file, documents, desk and reality tree each have a subclass.
